title: Sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) mediated adaptations to hypoxemic conditions in red blood cells (RBC) in acute and chronic respiratory diseases
summary: The aim of the present study is to investigate red blood cells/erythrocytes (Erys). Erys transport the oxygen you inhale from the lungs, the respiratory organs, to the organs that utilize oxygen (heart, brain, kidney, liver, etc.). It is now known that Erys can adapt to conditions associated with a different composition of our breathing air. You might be familiar with this phenomenon from a mountain vacation with "thin" air – experiencing shortness of breath. Indeed, people who live at high altitudes, such as the Alps, have more Erys in their blood than people who live at sea level, such as in the Netherlands. However, little is known about how our bodies adapt to these living conditions, and it is not well understood whether and how Erys adapt in diseases that prevent our bodies from taking in enough oxygen, such as pneumonia or a long-standing lung disease with airway narrowing (Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease, COPD). Therefore, we aim to examine the Erys in the laboratory and correlate and associate them with characteristics of the present disease. Furthermore, we want to investigate the function of the Erys, including their ability to transport oxygen.

interventions.name: Not interventional; Patients with acute and chronic respiratory diseases as well as those with Long-COVID-19 are being recruited. A healthy control will be recruited as well.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Acute respiratory disorder, Chronic respiratory disorder, COVID-19 post-recovery, healthy Participants
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of consent; Patients included in intervention studies; Patients < 18 years old; Moribund status
